answer: The cipher multiplier is published, charged in canyon, and quill lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 3 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 731 identities would post 2873 proofs and burn roughly 80 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
